chapter: Blue Devils, Moten and the Reno Club
title: The origin of 'One O'Clock Jump'
summary: Basie confirms the story: asked the title during a radio broadcast, he looked at the clock, and it became his theme because he did not have one.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: All right, so that's true then. "Another popular question is the origin of our theme 'One O'Clock Jump.'"
Well, he's getting ready to tell you.

Oh, this is true? "I'll answer that one right here, because it, too, has a very long connection with Kansas City. It also came out of one of our radio broadcasts." True? "Back in those days, when you went on the air, you didn't have to clear songs and titles --"
All that's true. I don't have to read it.
You don't have to even read it.
I don't have to read it?
No, because I know what it's going to say.
I know just exactly what he's going to say.
I started to playing something and he asked me what the title of it was. I said, "Wait a minute." I looked at the clock, right?
It was one o'clock. I take it, a.m.
All right. Why do you think -- why was that your theme? Why did that become your theme?
Did that become your theme right then?
Well, why did it become your theme?
Well, it's because I didn't have a theme.
Oh. All right. Well, why did that one become your theme? Just felt right probably.
Okay. 'It's unquestionably the record most closely associated with the band.'
